title: Which One? 了 vs 过, 不 vs 没, 在 before vs after the verb
description: A2 contrast practice: a specific past event or an experience, not (habit/decision) vs didn't/haven't, and where 在 + place goes.

points.title: 了 vs 过
points.summary: 了 = a specific action got done (and matters now). 过 = you have the experience (at least once, at some point).
points.body:
- 昨天我买**了**一件衣服，可是太小了 (that purchase, still relevant).
- 你吃**过**北京烤鸭吗? (ever?)
- 我去**过**日本 (I've been to Japan) ≠ 我去**了**日本 (I went to Japan — maybe still there).

points.title: 不 vs 没 (A2)
points.summary: 不: habits, wishes, decisions, 'not anymore' (不…了). 没: didn't, haven't (yet) (还没).
points.body:
- 我昨天**没**去，今天也**不**想去.
- 他现在**不**抽**了**.
- 我还**没**想好.
examples: I didn't go yesterday, and I don't want to go today either.

points.title: 在 + place: before or after the verb?
points.summary: Normally 在 + place goes **before** the verb (在图书馆看书). Only with 住, 坐, 站, 放 (where something ends up / stays) does it go **after** (住在北京).
points.body:
- 他**在**图书馆看书.
- 他**住在**北京.
- ~~他看书在图书馆~~ ✗

questions.prompt: {你|nǐ}{吃|chī}（　）{北京|Běijīng}{烤鸭|kǎoyā}{吗|ma}？{没|méi}{吃|chī}{过|guo}{的话|dehuà}，{我们|wǒmen}{去|qù}{吃|chī}{吧|ba}！
notes: 吃了吗 = 'did you eat it (just now)' — the follow-up asks about experience.
questions.translation: Have you ever had Peking duck? If not, let's go and have some!

questions.prompt: {昨天|zuótiān}{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}（　）{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yīfu}，{可是|kěshì}{太|tài}{小|xiǎo}{了|le}，{今天|jīntiān}{要|yào}{去|qù}{换|huàn}。
notes: 过 is for experiences — not one specific purchase you're still dealing with.
questions.translation: I bought a piece of clothing yesterday, but it's too small — I'm going to exchange it today.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means 'I've been to Japan (before)'?
notes: 去日本了 = 'I've gone to Japan' (maybe still there).
去了日本 = 'I went to Japan' (a specific trip).
昨天 is a past event — 没.
questions.translation: I didn't go yesterday, and I don't want to go today either.
He used to smoke, but he doesn't anymore.

notes: 还不想好 isn't grammatical — 想好 is a result.
questions.translation: I haven't decided yet — give me a moment.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means 'He lives in Beijing'?
notes: 在住 would mean 'is living (right now)', and 北京 can't follow like that.
在 needs the place after it.
在 needs the place after it.

questions.prompt: {我们|wǒmen}{明天|míngtiān}（　）{那|nà}{家|jiā}{咖啡馆|kāfēiguǎn}{见面|jiànmiàn}{吧|ba}。
questions.explanation: Place before the verb: **在 + place + 见面**.
notes: 坐在…见面 = 'sit in … meet' — two verbs clash.
questions.translation: Let's meet at that café tomorrow.

notes: 看 doesn't take 在 after it.
English order — 在 + place goes before the verb.
The place can't come at the end.
